project.project_title: Print Designer needed — production artwork files for luxury pareo brand

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

Thank you so much for getting back to me!

Right now, we’re leaning towards digital printing, particularly for pareos and textile accessories. The broader aesthetic is refined, artisanal, and centred on luxury resort wear, with natural textures, woven influences, and imperfect detailing rather than anything overly polished or graphic.

I’ve attached the reference images to give you a clearer idea of the diagonal basket weave direction and the overall mood. We definitely want the result to feel organic, elevated, and textural rather than flat.

We’re hoping these can be enlarged, or used as inspiration, to develop our own textile print. IS that something that can be done? We’d also like to make 2 x block colour pareos using the mustard / burgandy shades from the attached reference, along with the black border. However, we’re keen to have your help with the Zebra & woven print first.

We completely understand the timing as well. Quality is our priority, so we’d prefer to allow enough time for the final files to feel thoughtful and fully production ready.

Please let me know your thoughts.

value_updates.deliverable: Custom zebra textile print developed from the supplied reference imagery
aesthetic_direction: natural and imperfect rather than overly polished or graphic

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
I’m so glad I found you!!

Everything you’ve described sounds fantastic and completely in line with what we want. I especially love the plan to create the texture manually, as that will keep it feeling elevated and organic instead of too digital.

Let’s start with the zebra and basket weave, and once those are approved, we can move on to the block colour pareos. I can confirm the Pantone colours for you as well, although you may be able to identify them from the image.

The fabric will probably be cotton voile, with silk/cotton voile also a possibility depending on the final sampling. I’ll verify the exact fabrication with the supplier soon.

I can’t wait to see the first check-in!!

value_updates.stripe_treatment: bold, fluid and gestural rather than flat
value_updates.development_sequence: develop the zebra print before the block-colour pareos

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hey [FREELANCER_NAME_002],

Perfect, everything sounds excellent!

I completely understand the limitations around matching the Pantones, and I’m happy for you to begin with a visual approximation before we refine it once production confirms the final Pantones. That approach makes complete sense.

For the basket weave, we’re picturing each diamond at approximately 5cm diagonally across the repeat. We’d also like a very very fine mustard edge outlining the woven detail.

For the zebra print, we’d like a black edge/border surrounding the design.

I’ve attached a PDF containing the mockups and some extra references for you to use as well.

I know the current quote covers the two patterns, so we can start with those and assess the additional designs afterwards. However, could you confirm whether the other two block versions are also covered by this quote? I’ve included the Pantone colours we’d like to use for the terracotta and mustard tones, so please let me know whether that’s possible for you.

I’ll ask the supplier about the ICC colour profile too and send it over if one is available!! I’ll also go onto Upwork shortly and activate the contract so we can officially get started.

value_updates.border_treatment: black edge or border around the design

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001]!

I’ve attached the Milestone 1 PDF containing every print developed to date. Below is an overview of what’s included and the information I need from you before proceeding.

1\. Contents of this delivery
The Basket Weave print is presented in two texture versions, Frottage and Reference-Based, with two scales for each. The Zebra print includes three directional options—Noir, Savanna, and Gold Skin—each displayed both as a tile detail and at full repeat scale. There are also two block colour pareos, Rooibos Tea and Sudan Brown, and each is shown with two border scale choices, Slim and Full. For reference, every mockup is displayed at 110 x 180 cm.

You can review the full resolution repeat files here: [URL_001]

2\. Selections I need from you
Please tell me which Zebra direction you prefer: 01 Noir, 02 Savanna, or 03 Gold Skin. I also need to know whether you favour the Frottage or Reference-Based Basket Weave texture. For the block colour pareos, please choose whether Slim or Full is the better border scale for your collection. When reviewing the options, use the measurements provided in the PDF, as they represent the actual scale on fabric.

3\. Colour appearance on screen compared with fabric
The warm golden shades, particularly those in the Gold Skin zebra option, will look slightly more matte once printed on fabric than they do on a screen. This is a normal result of pigment printing on voile rather than any reduction in quality; it is simply how that material displays colour. I wanted to clarify this ahead of production to prevent any surprises.

4\. Details required before I prepare the final files
I’ll need confirmation of your fabric supplier’s ICC profile so I can calibrate the CMYK files. If available, please also confirm the precise Pantone references with your supplier. I need the final seam allowance measurements that should be incorporated into the digital production files, along with any further notes or changes for the chosen prints.

5\. Milestone 2 schedule
After receiving your selections and feedback, I’ll work towards May 29 as the Milestone 2 deadline. Should everything be completed sooner, I’ll deliver it ahead of that date.

I’m looking forward to hearing your feedback!
[FREELANCER_NAME_002]

execution.observed_behavior: Freelancer reports developing Noir, Savanna and Gold Skin zebra directions and providing each at tile-detail and full-repeat scale for review.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Would it be all right for us to send the amends on Monday? Please let me know whether that timing suits you.

I have a few minor colour changes in mind. The Zebra feels slightly too gold, so I’d like it to be lighter. For the weave, I prefer the 7.5cm option you showed, although that could also be a little lighter. It would be helpful to see it with the border too.

I already have my feedback, but I want to review it with her so our instructions are completely clear.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hey [FREELANCER_NAME_002],

Thank you for preparing all of these. The direction is definitely moving closer, although I have several colour and scale refinements that I think will make everything feel softer, more elevated, and more TELA MARE.

Based on the references we provided, our goal was a naturally aged, tonal effect. Right now, the artwork feels a little too saturated and clean. We’d like to add softness, irregularity, and depth so the prints read as textural and collected rather than overly graphic.

In general, both prints could use:
\* reduced contrast
\* additional grain
\* a stronger texture overlay
\* edges that are slightly more faded
\* less of a “perfect vector” appearance

Zebra print:
\* At present, the zebra feels somewhat too yellow/gold and the contrast is a little high.
\* I’d prefer the gold to be reduced and shifted towards a softer bronze / sandy caramel shade.
\* The overall result should look sun-faded, vintage, and expensive, rather than bright or excessively golden.
\* The larger stripe direction with the more organic character feels strongest to me.

Weave print:
\* The current weave is leaning a little too orange/red.
\* I’d like to move it towards a softer brushed brown with greater depth and less warmth.
\* We prefer the larger 5cm diagonal weave scale, so ideally we would combine:
→ the colour/tone used in the smaller weave
→ with the larger scale from the 5cm option.

Overall, the designs can be a bit softer, more tonal, and more lived-in—less saturated and polished, and more earthy, natural, and collected.

Once the tones are refined, I think we’ll be very close!

value_updates.colour_tone: soft bronze or sandy caramel rather than yellow or gold

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001]!

I’ve attached the Milestone 1 PDF containing every print developed to date. Below is an overview of what’s included and the information I need from you before proceeding.

1\. Contents of this delivery
The Basket Weave print is presented in two texture versions, Frottage and Reference-Based, with two scales for each. The Zebra print includes three directional options—Noir, Savanna, and Gold Skin—each displayed both as a tile detail and at full repeat scale. There are also two block colour pareos, Rooibos Tea and Sudan Brown, and each is shown with two border scale choices, Slim and Full. For reference, every mockup is displayed at 110 x 180 cm.

You can review the full resolution repeat files here: [URL_001]

2\. Selections I need from you
Please tell me which Zebra direction you prefer: 01 Noir, 02 Savanna, or 03 Gold Skin. I also need to know whether you favour the Frottage or Reference-Based Basket Weave texture. For the block colour pareos, please choose whether Slim or Full is the better border scale for your collection. When reviewing the options, use the measurements provided in the PDF, as they represent the actual scale on fabric.

3\. Colour appearance on screen compared with fabric
The warm golden shades, particularly those in the Gold Skin zebra option, will look slightly more matte once printed on fabric than they do on a screen. This is a normal result of pigment printing on voile rather than any reduction in quality; it is simply how that material displays colour. I wanted to clarify this ahead of production to prevent any surprises.

4\. Details required before I prepare the final files
I’ll need confirmation of your fabric supplier’s ICC profile so I can calibrate the CMYK files. If available, please also confirm the precise Pantone references with your supplier. I need the final seam allowance measurements that should be incorporated into the digital production files, along with any further notes or changes for the chosen prints.

5\. Milestone 2 schedule
After receiving your selections and feedback, I’ll work towards May 29 as the Milestone 2 deadline. Should everything be completed sooner, I’ll deliver it ahead of that date.

I’m looking forward to hearing your feedback!
[FREELANCER_NAME_002]
